target: Das Kind will auf keinen Fall Spinat essen.
english: The child doesn't want to eat spinach under any circumstances.
tip: 'Auf keinen Fall' – 'under no circumstances' – emphatic refusal.

target: Meine Familie feiert Weihnachten traditionell mit Kartoffelsalat und Würstchen.
english: My family traditionally celebrates Christmas with potato salad and sausages.
tip: 'feiern' – stem-final '-r' + '-n'; regular: 'feiert'.

target: Er muss seinen Pass bei der Botschaft verlängern lassen.
english: He has to have his passport renewed at the embassy.
tip: 'muss' (modal) pushes 'lassen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich will meine Angst vor öffentlichem Sprechen endlich überwinden.
english: I want to finally overcome my fear of public speaking.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'berwinden' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Wir wollen den Jahrestag mit einem besonderen Abendessen feiern.
english: We want to celebrate the anniversary with a special dinner.
tip: 'wollen' (modal) pushes 'feiern' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Sie darf nach der Operation drei Wochen lang nicht fliegen.
english: She may not fly for three weeks after the operation.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'fliegen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Wir müssen die alte Heizungsanlage noch vor dem Winter erneuern.
english: We have to replace the old heating system before winter.
tip: 'müssen' (modal) pushes 'erneuern' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Um Viertel nach acht fahre ich mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.
english: At quarter past eight I take the bus to work.
tip: 'Viertel nach' = quarter past. 'Viertel vor' = quarter to.

target: Frag doch einfach den freundlichen Herrn an der Rezeption nach dem Weg.
english: Just ask the friendly gentleman at the reception for directions.
tip: Adjective 'freundlichen' – its ending depends on the article type, case, and noun gender. After definite articles, usually -e or -en.

target: Das Stipendium ermöglicht der Studentin ein Auslandssemester.
english: The scholarship enables the student to study abroad for a semester.
tip: 'Auslandssemester' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Er möchte seinen Kindern eine mehrsprachige Erziehung ermöglichen.
english: He would like to enable a multilingual education for his children.
tip: Accusative reflexive: sich waschen, sich freuen, sich setzen.

target: Der Supermarkt liegt zwischen der Post und dem Rathaus.
english: The supermarket is between the post office and the town hall.
tip: 'Zwischen' + dative: location – 'zwischen der Post und dem Rathaus'.

target: Sie will unbedingt den neuen Film im Kino sehen.
english: She absolutely wants to see the new film at the cinema.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'sehen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du willst doch nicht ernsthaft bei diesem Wetter joggen?
english: You don't seriously want to jog in this weather, do you?
tip: 'willst' (modal) pushes 'joggen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du musst die Medikamente dreimal täglich nach dem Essen nehmen.
english: You have to take the medication three times daily after eating.
tip: 'musst' (modal) pushes 'nehmen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er kommt heute nicht zur Arbeit, weil er krank ist.
english: He is not coming to work today because he is sick.
tip: 'Nicht' negates verbs and adjectives – placed before what it negates.

target: Er trägt weder eine Jacke noch einen Schal bei dieser Kälte.
english: He wears neither a jacket nor a scarf despite the cold.
tip: 'denn' is a coordinating conjunction – does not change word order.

target: Ich möchte an der Exkursion zum Schwarzwald teilnehmen.
english: I would like to participate in the excursion to the Black Forest.
tip: 'sich' always comes after the conjugated verb in main clauses.

target: Die Harfenistin probte das Stück vor dem leeren Konzertsaal.
english: The harpist rehearsed the piece in front of the empty concert hall.
tip: Adjective 'leeren' – its ending depends on the article type, case, and noun gender. After definite articles, usually -e or -en.

target: Ich rate meiner Schwester, vor dem Urlaub eine Reiseversicherung abzuschließen.
english: I advise my sister to take out travel insurance before the vacation.
tip: 'Reiseversicherung' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Ich trinke abends keinen Kaffee, sonst kann ich nicht einschlafen.
english: I don't drink coffee in the evening, otherwise I can't fall asleep.
tip: 'Nicht' vs 'kein': use 'keinen Kaffee' (negating noun) but 'nicht einschlafen' (negating verb).

target: Wir würden es begrüßen, wenn Sie sich zeitnah zu dem Angebot äußern könnten.
english: We would welcome it if you could express your views on the offer soon.
tip: Subordinate clause = comma + conjunction + …everything… + verb. Verb is the final word, separated by no comma from the rest.

target: Ich darf an meinem Geburtstag ausnahmsweise länger aufbleiben.
english: I am allowed to stay up later on my birthday as an exception.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'aufbleiben' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: In dieser ruhigen Bibliothek darf man auf keinen Fall laut telefonieren.
english: In this quiet library, one must not talk loudly on the phone under any circumstances.
tip: 'auf keinen Fall' = 'under no circumstances'; emphatic negation.

target: Ich will dieses Semester mindestens drei Kurse an der Volkshochschule belegen.
english: I want to take at least three courses at the adult education center this semester.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'belegen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Servus, wie läuft es bei dir?
english: Hi, how's it going?
tip: 'Servus' is common in Bavaria and Austria – both greeting and farewell.

target: Wir nähern uns dem Ziel.
english: We are approaching the goal.
tip: 'Sich nähern' + dative = to approach.

target: Er steht hinter dem Zaun.
english: He stands behind the fence.
tip: 'Hinter' + dative for location.

target: Wir können morgen schwimmen gehen.
english: We can go swimming tomorrow.
tip: 'können' (modal) pushes 'gehen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Wir können das morgen besprechen.
english: We can discuss that tomorrow.
tip: 'können' (modal) pushes 'besprechen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Grüß Gott, darf ich mich vorstellen?
english: Hello, may I introduce myself?
tip: 'Grüß Gott' is the standard greeting in southern Germany and Austria.

target: Wir wohnen gegenüber dem Park.
english: We live across from the park.
tip: 'über' (over/about) + dative = location. Accusative would indicate direction/movement toward.

target: Ich muss heute länger arbeiten.
english: I have to work longer today.
tip: 'muss' (modal) pushes 'arbeiten' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich muss noch einkaufen gehen.
english: I still have to go shopping.
tip: 'muss' (modal) pushes 'gehen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er will nicht mehr warten.
english: He doesn't want to wait anymore.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'warten' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich will heute Abend ausgehen.
english: I want to go out tonight.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'ausgehen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du kannst sehr gut Klavier spielen.
english: You can play piano very well.
tip: 'kannst' (modal) pushes 'spielen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du darfst hier leider nicht parken.
english: Unfortunately you may not park here.
tip: 'darfst' (modal) pushes 'parken' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er kann sehr gut Klavier spielen.
english: He can play piano very well.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'spielen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er kann das Problem allein lösen.
english: He can solve the problem alone.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'sen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er nähert sich dem scheuen Reh vorsichtig.
english: He cautiously approaches the shy deer.
tip: Dative: 'sich nähern' takes dative – 'dem scheuen Reh'.

target: Sie antwortet dem Professor auf seine schwierige Frage.
english: She answers the professor's difficult question.
tip: Dative: 'antworten' takes dative for the person – 'dem Professor'.

target: Er kann sich leider nicht an den Namen erinnern.
english: Unfortunately he cannot remember the name.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'erinnern' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich möchte mich kurz vorstellen.
english: I would like to briefly introduce myself.
tip: 'Möchte' (would like) is the polite way to express wants – used much more than 'wollen' in everyday speech.

target: Darf ich Ihnen meinen Kollegen vorstellen?
english: May I introduce my colleague to you?
tip: Formal introductions use 'Ihnen' (dative of 'Sie').

target: Die Farbe der Blumen ist wunderschön.
english: The color of the flowers is beautiful.
tip: Dative changes articles: der→dem, die→der, das→dem, die(pl)→den(+n). Mastering these transforms is essential.

target: Die Kosten des Projekts sind hoch.
english: The costs of the project are high.
tip: 'des Projekts' – genitive case showing possession. Masculine/neuter nouns add -s or -es.

target: Die Regeln des Spiels sind einfach.
english: The rules of the game are simple.
tip: 'des Spiels' – genitive case showing possession. Masculine/neuter nouns add -s or -es.

target: Das Ziel unserer Reise ist München.
english: The destination of our trip is Munich.
tip: Dative changes 'ein/mein/sein' to 'einem/meinem/seinem' (masc/neut) and 'einer/meiner/seiner' (fem).

target: Wir treffen uns vor dem Kino.
english: We meet in front of the cinema.
tip: 'uns' – reflexive pronoun for 'treffen'. German requires it even when English doesn't (e.g., 'sich freuen' = 'to be happy').

target: Sie möchte gern in Wien wohnen.
english: She would like to live in Vienna.
tip: 'Möchte' is the subjunctive of 'mögen'.

target: Wir müssen die Miete pünktlich zahlen.
english: We must pay the rent on time.
tip: 'müssen' (modal) pushes 'zahlen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich gebe dem Kellner ein großzügiges Trinkgeld.
english: I give the waiter a generous tip.
tip: Dative: 'der Kellner' → 'dem Kellner'. Masculine/neuter articles change to 'dem' in dative.

target: Er traut seinem eigenen Urteil nicht immer.
english: He doesn't always trust his own judgment.
tip: Dative: 'trauen' takes dative – 'seinem eigenen Urteil'.

target: Das Ergebnis entspricht den Erwartungen der Geschäftsführung.
english: The result meets the expectations of management.
tip: Dative: 'entsprechen' takes dative – 'den Erwartungen'.

target: Sie gehorcht ihren strengen Eltern ohne Widerspruch.
english: She obeys her strict parents without protest.
tip: 'ohne' (without) always takes accusative – no exceptions.

target: Ich vertraue meiner Intuition bei schwierigen Entscheidungen.
english: I trust my intuition with difficult decisions.
tip: 'Entscheidungen' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Er kann fließend Deutsch und Französisch sprechen.
english: He can speak German and French fluently.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'sprechen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du solltest mehr Obst und Gemüse essen.
english: You should eat more fruit and vegetables.
tip: 'Solltest' is Konjunktiv II of 'sollen' – softer, advisory tone.

target: Ich muss heute Abend unbedingt noch einkaufen gehen.
english: I absolutely have to go shopping tonight.
tip: Reciprocal 'sich': wir treffen uns = we meet each other.
